title: Hybrid redispatch playbook for dedicated capacity shortfalls and scaling regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During a production incident on 2026-02-25 we observed sustained throughput shortfalls for multiple Dedicated customers over a 45 minute window. Autoscaler signals were delayed and the fleet did not open sufficient headroom; requests queued and downstream latency SLOs were violated for customers on mid-tier Dedicated pools.

Why this ticket exists:
We need a practical, testable playbook that operators and on-call engineers can run to restore capacity quickly (minutes) while we investigate root cause and implement long-term fixes. The playbook must combine immediate mitigations (temporary redispatch to hosted/ephemeral pools, emergency scaling overrides) with safeguards (cost guardrails, customer routing rules, step-down rollback). It must also include postmortem action items with owners and measurable acceptance criteria.

Incident timeline (brief):
- 2026-02-25 13:04 UTC: Alert: dedicated-pool-03 queue depth rising; error rate increases reported by SLO monitor.
- 13:06 UTC: Autoscale attempted to add nodes but API returned a stalled response; scale actions not applied due to controller health flapping.
- 13:11 UTC: Traffic continued to exceed capacity -> per-route latency > 3x SLO for 18 minutes.
- 13:30 UTC: On-call manually triggered conservative redispatch to hosted runtime for affected customers; visible recovery by 13:40 UTC.
- 13:50 UTC: Emergency mitigation completed; incident declared mitigated at 13:52 UTC.

Preliminary root cause (investigation notes):
- A recent autoscaler change (ENG-17203 rollout) tightened the concurrency threshold and introduced a backoff that, combined with a controller gc job running concurrently, delayed the controller's reconciliation loop by ~90s in some nodes.
- Telemetry sampling bug in the controller-agent (dropped ~30% of queue-depth samples) caused the autoscaler to undervalue demand when combined with the backoff.
- No automatic fallback path existed to shift traffic to compatible hosted variants when Dedicated pools signaled degraded health.

Immediate goals for playbook (operational):
1) Restore customer throughput within 10 minutes using the smallest-cost, lowest-risk interventions.
2) Prevent SLA breaches by automatically enabling fallback routing for affected routes when dedicated pool signals indicate degraded health.
3) Provide clear operator steps for escalation, rollback, and post-incident reconciliation.

Playbook steps (operator-facing):
A) Triage & quick checks (0-3 minutes):
  - Confirm alerts: review dedicated pool queue depth, node utilization, autoscaler reconciliation errors in metrics dashboard (link in attachments).
  - If controller reconciliation lag > 60s and queue depth rising, mark pool as degraded and escalate to on-call infra.

B) Fast redispatch (3-10 minutes):
  - Run redispatch script (scripts/redispatch/hybrid-redispatch.sh) to reroute traffic for affected customer route IDs to: 1) compatible hosted model variant (same model family, lower token limits) AND 2) ephemeral burst pool (if enabled). The script should attach a transient header X-RW-Fallback:dedicated-redispatch for observability.
  - Enable emergency-scale override: apply manual scale-up of +20% capacity to the dedicated pool via API (admin-only). Document the API call in audit logs and Slack #dedicated-ops.
  - Apply temporary rate-limiter at route level to preserve fairness if redispatch is not immediately available.

C) Stabilize & observe (10-45 minutes):
  - Monitor end-to-end latency per route; rollback redispatch only after 2 consecutive 5-minute windows below SLO threshold.
  - Keep emergency-scale override in place until autoscaler controller recovers and produces stable reconciliation for 30 minutes.

D) Post-incident actions (owner + deadlines):
  - Fix autoscaler controller bug (ENG-17203-revert/patch): owner Ethan Cole, due 2026-03-04. Acceptance: consistent reconciliation latency < 30s in staging with synthetic burst test.
  - Telemetry patch to prevent sample drops (ENG-XXXXXX): owner Priya Singh, due 2026-03-10. Acceptance: <1% sample loss in agent test harness.
  - Implement automated fallback-routing policy (policy design + rollout): owner Liam O'Connor, due 2026-03-17. Acceptance: can transparently route to hosted variant with <=5% quality regression (tracked by eval set).
  - Add cost-guardrail to redispatch script to limit daily spillover per customer to $X and send alerts when threshold approaching: owner Finance/Platform coord, due 2026-03-20.

Longer-term engineering work (program level):
- Add enrichment to capacity signals: combine queue depth + p99 token-latency + node-level headroom estimate so autoscaler reacts earlier. (ENG-42319).
- Document a canary toggling plan so autoscaler controller changes are ramped with automated rollback if queue-depth variance increases above threshold. (Integrate with canary-ops).

Acceptance criteria for playbook rollout:
- On-call runbook test within staging that completes full redispatch and recovery within <8 minutes for a 3x synthetic traffic spike.
- New automated fallback policy triggers in staging and preserves SLOs for simulated Dedicated outages.
- Postmortem and action items owner assignments completed and tracked in this ticket and downstream issues.

Notes on trade-offs and risks:
- Redispatching to hosted variants can increase customer costs and slightly degrade model output quality. The playbook includes thresholds and a daily cost cap to limit exposure.
- Aggressive emergency scaling risks oscillation if autoscaler bug persists; ensure manual overrides are bounded and audited.

Links and artifacts are in attachments. The script referenced must be added to the repo under infra/ops-scripts with an accompanying test harness.

This ticket is the canonical playbook; sub-issues will track code patches, telemetry fixes, runbook tests, and customer communications.
